label: conj:wigner-axiom
title: The Wigner axiom: a one-dimensional classical-limit obstruction
html:
Conjecture. The Wigner axiom: a one-dimensional classical-limit obstruction

Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe with archimedean base curve M_0, and let \mathrm{Obs}(\mathbf{C}, q \to 1) = HH^2(\mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{g}), \mathrm{Ad}) be its classical limit obstruction.

Conjecture (the Wigner axiom). The classical-limit obstruction space is one-dimensional, and its generator is realised by the Euler class of the base:

(W1) \dim_k \mathrm{Obs}(\mathbf{C}, q \to 1) = 1;

(W2) the archimedean realisation \mathrm{Obs}(\mathbf{C}, q \to 1) \to H^2(M_0; k) carries a generator w(A) onto the Euler class e(TM_0), which is non-zero; consequently \langle e(TM_0), [M_0] \rangle = \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) = 2 - 2g(M_0) is the integer that determines the obstruction.

Why it is an axiom. Two arguments that were offered for (W1) do not go through. The first invoked Poincaré duality for Hochschild cohomology in the untwisted form HH^{2} \cong (HH^{1})^{\vee}; for the Hopf algebras in question the duality that holds is Brown and Zhang's twisted form HH^{i}(H, M) \cong HH_{d-i}(H, {}_{\nu}M) [brown-zhang-2008], cohomology to homology with the Nakayama automorphism \nu on the coefficients, and at q \neq 1 the untwisted version fails outright: the top Hochschild homology of \mathcal{O}_q(\mathrm{SL}_2) drops, and the one-dimensional top group reappears only after the twist [hadfield-krahmer-2005]. The second counted the deformation direction q as a class in the obstruction space; it is a class in HH^{1}, one degree lower. And at the classical point the statement is false: for \mathfrak{g} semisimple and M finite-dimensional, Whitehead's lemmas give H^{1}(\mathfrak{g}, M) = H^{2}(\mathfrak{g}, M) = 0 [weibel1994], so \mathrm{Obs} = 0 at q = 1. One-dimensionality at q \neq 1 is therefore a hypothesis about the substrate, not a theorem of the axioms.

Why (W2) has this target. For Bring's surface the symmetry group S_5 acts on everything in sight, and an equivariant realisation must land in the S_5-invariant part of the base's Hochschild theory. That invariant part is k^2 in HH_0 — spanned by H^0(M_0, \mathcal{O}) and H^1(M_0, K) = H^2(M_0; k) — and k in HH^0, and it is zero in HH^2(M_0) = H^1(TM_0), the deformation space of the curve. An equivariant image of a one-dimensional obstruction space among the deformations of the base is therefore zero, and the only invariant line that can carry the integer is H^2(M_0; k), where the Euler class lives. The axiom is stated with that target and no other.

What it buys and what would refute it. Every block that reduces a Millennium-type persistence question to the divisibility n \mid \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) is conditional on this axiom; the reduction itself (obstruction reduction) is then a theorem. A computation of HH^{2}(\mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2), \mathrm{Ad}) at generic q with dimension different from one refutes (W1); an equivariant realisation whose image of the obstruction line vanishes in H^2(M_0; k) refutes (W2). Neither computation exists in this paper.

The name follows Wigner's Courant lecture of 11 May 1959 on the unreasonable effectiveness of mathematics [wigner1960]: the axiom is exactly the assumption that a single scalar of the substrate governs the persistence of its structure into the classical world.
